items.text: PITCH ENVELOPE double click adds or remo

items.tip: Back to the simple curve made by Start, Sweep and Curve.

items.text: Free B0 C1 C#1 D1 D#1 E1 F1 F#1 G1 G#1 A
items.tip: Pick the root note of your track. The tail pitch snaps to it. Use the Tail knob for fine tuning.
Click to snap Tail to the exact note shown (0 ct). Example: F1 +45 ct becomes F1 0 ct.
The pitch the kick settles on. Tune it to the root note of your track so kick and sub bass add up instead of fighting. A1 is 55 Hz, F#1 is 46.25 Hz.

items.text: Off C C# D D# E F F# G G# A A# B
items.tip: Pick the root note of your bassline. The chip below tells you if the kick tail sits on it, on its fifth, or clashes with it. A clash makes the low end muddy.
Pitch at the very first moment. A high start (about 800 to 1000 Hz) gives the snap.
How fast the pitch falls from Start to Tail. About 25 to 35 ms is tight. Around 80 ms starts to sound like a laser.
Shape of the fall. 1.00 is exponential. Lower drops faster at the start, higher drops slower at the start.

Lets the low body of the kick grow over the first milliseconds instead of starting at full level. Real trance kicks start with a quiet, fast pitch drop and the click on top, then the body swells in. 40 ms is typical. 0 is off.
Spectrum of the first 370 ms of the kick, in dB.
Load a kick you like (.wav) as a reference. Its spectrum is drawn in amber over ours so you can see the difference. You can also drop a file on the spectrum.
Smooth symmetric saturation. Adds harmonics so the kick is heard on small speakers. Level is matched, so it does not just get louder.
Asymmetric saturation with even harmonics and extra low weight.
Smooth fuzz stage. Keep low for clean kicks, push for hard dance.
Soft clipper at the end. More clip makes the kick denser and louder without going over 0 dB.
Save the finished kick as a 24-bit mono .wav file on your computer (inside this web preview it arrives zipped). You can also drag the waveform straight into your DAW.
Drag this waveform into your DAW or a folder to drop the kick as a .wav file. Or use Export .wav.
Loudness of the click, the short high knock that lets you hear the kick inside a wall of supersaws.
Centre frequency of the click. Roughly 2 to 5 kHz cuts through leads.
How long the click lasts. Longer clicks sound harder and more clicky.
Extra punch in the first tens of milliseconds, while the pitch is still falling through the chest range.
Level of the tail that sits on the Tail pitch. This is the low weight you feel.
Keeps the kick at full level for a few ms before it decays, so the top of the hit lands harder.
Time from the end of Hold until the kick is silent (-60 dB). The marker on the waveform shows one 16th note at your tempo.
Shape of the decay. 1.0 fades steadily from the start. Higher keeps the kick near full level for most of its length, then drops fast at the end. Real trance kicks sit around 4 to 5.
Output level in dB. Watch the meter on the right.
True-peak ceiling in dB. If the kick would go above this after conversion (inter-sample peaks), it is turned down to sit exactly on it. -0.3 dB is safe for any export.
Flip the polarity of the kick. If the kick and the bass cancel each other and the low end sounds thin, flip one of them and compare.
Phase align. Flips a layer upside down if it starts against the body, so click, attack and body push the same way and the punch is the same every time.
True peak in dB (inter-sample peaks included). Stays under the Ceiling.
Average level of the first 120 ms. This is the loudness you feel. Sauce raises it while the peak stays put.
K-weighted loudness of the loudest 400 ms, in LUFS. A quick way to compare two kicks by loudness.
Glue compressor and limiter.
Render the finished kick, see all of it, save it as a .wav or drag it into your DAW.

How much of the glue compressor is blended in. 0 is off. Shape it with Threshold, Ratio, Attack and Release. Works even when Sauce Amount is 0. Fills the gaps in the tail so the kick feels thick and solid.
Where the glue compressor starts working, in dB below the kick peak. Lower means more of the kick gets squeezed.
How hard it squeezes above the threshold. 2 is gentle, 6 is firm, 20 is almost a limiter.
How slowly the compressor grabs. Longer lets more of the click and punch through first. Try 30 to 50 ms for a hard punch.
How fast it lets go. Short brings the tail up between beats, long keeps it smooth.
How hard the limiter is pushed. It raises the kick, then stops the peaks from growing, so the body gets louder and punchier.
Peak level of the kick going into the glue compressor, in dB.
Most gain reduction the glue compressor applied, in dB.
Turn the limiter on or off. It pushes the kick louder without letting the peaks grow, a quick way to a punchy drum.

items.text: SAUCE Weight, punch, crack and loudness

items.tip: Master amount of the Sauce chain. 0 is off. Raise it to blend in all the stages at once, then shape them with the knobs next to it.
Saturates the sub below 120 Hz so the low note grows harmonics at 2 and 3 times its pitch. Gives weight you can hear on laptop speakers, and a little more low level.
A soft swell in the low tail at about 40 to 80 ms. Makes the kick breathe and pump, so the tail lifts after the hit instead of just dying away.
Saturates the 120 to 800 Hz band in parallel. That is where a kick is felt in the chest on small and large speakers. More punch, more body.
Lifts and rounds the top band above 800 Hz, strongest in the first 10 ms. Sharper attack that cuts through a full mix.
Makes the kick denser and louder while the peak stays the same: up to 6 dB more average level, with the peaks shaved smoothly instead of hard clipped.
Cuts the boxy zone around 250 Hz, up to 12 dB. That is where kicks sound cardboard or cheap.
Wide boost around 80 Hz, up to 8 dB. The part you feel in your chest.
Boosts everything above 2.5 kHz, up to 15 dB. Brings out the click so the kick cuts through.

Loudness of layer A.
Pitch of layer A in semitones. Built-in sounds move their tone or filter. Your own sound plays faster or slower.
Trims the first ms off a sound, to cut silence or a soft attack. Fine range 0 to 40 ms; hold Shift while dragging for even finer steps.
How long the layer lasts. For built-in sounds it is the decay time. For your own sound it is the part that plays, with a short fade at the end.
Starts the layer this many ms after the kick. Use it to line the top up with the body of the kick.
High-pass filter. Cuts the lows of the layer so it does not fight the sub. At 20 Hz it is off.
Low-pass filter. Softens the highs of the layer. At 20 kHz it is off.

Same kick: every key plays exactly the kick you set, whatever key you press.
Pitched: each key retunes the whole kick to that note, so it plays up or down the keyboard.

Loop one kick per beat at the tempo on the right.
Tempo used by the loop and the timing readout. 138 is the default.
Adds a simple rolling bass on the 16th notes after each kick, one octave above the tail note, so you can hear how kick and bass sit together.
